text:
Lawson Crouse is doing almost everything right except the part that goes on the scoreboard. Two goals in 22 games looks like a slump, but he has 5.1 expected goals, and with him on the ice at five on five Utah gets nearly 59% of the chance quality. He's shooting 5.3% against a usual rate around 13 or 14%. That gap tends to close, and his chances say he hasn't lost anything.

The Sheriff is still the Sheriff: 55 hits, 17 blocks and a role that grew late in this stretch, near 19 minutes in two of his last three games. Last season Evolving-Hockey had him worth 1.4 wins, 110th among forwards, mostly from even-strength offense, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking flagged a passing quirk: 18% of his setups cross the royal road, against 7% for a typical forward.

The problem for Utah is timing. The Mammoth have lost eight of their last ten, four of them by one goal or in overtime, and a power forward with 24 goals last season is exactly the finishing they're missing.
